acceptance: ADR file exists in _project/decisions/ with D1-D12 each marked decided or deferred-to-gate, with rationale
Global guardrails and abandon criteria copied verbatim into the ADR
Repo owner approval recorded in the ADR (name + date); without it no astro-site-* item may be taken
ADR cross-references dlv2-60, dlv2-62, ci-dedupe-11 and adr-independent-publication-authorities and states the ordering constraints
context:
GLOBAL GUARDRAILS (apply to every astro-site-* item):
G-a No change to production deploy wiring until dlv2-62 is done; the site plugs into site-deploy, never into publication-deploy.yml.
G-b docs/ is the single editable content source until the cutover PR. No dual editing.
G-c URL parity: zero URLs from the inventory (astro-site-01) may go missing. Any approved exception needs a static redirect page.
G-d Explorer behaviour is frozen during the migration. Its vitest, jest-axe and Playwright suites stay green; only path and config edits are allowed.
G-e Required checks are never weakened. A new or swapped required context lands in the same PR as its drift guard (AGENTS.md CI policy). The visual gate keeps the ci-dedupe-11 exact-base-SHA semantics.
G-f COMMENT-POLICY-001 applies to TS, Astro and CSS: no explanatory comments or docstrings. Run make comment-policy-check.
G-g No new third-party runtime scripts, analytics or CDN assets; fonts are self-hosted or system. Prism moves off cdnjs.
G-h npm audit:high clean; exact lockfile; check_artifact_privacy.py passes on every assembled artifact.
G-i One PR per item to develop, merged through the queue; no stacked PRs.
G-j Do not commit screenshots or generated binaries.
ABANDON if spike gate G1 fails, or if parity (astro-site-50) cannot reach zero missing URLs without redirects for more than 5% of pages.
description:
Gate G0. No other astro-site-* item may start until this ADR is approved by the repo owner.

Write _project/decisions/adr-astro-unified-site.md. It must decide each of the following, giving the default below or a reasoned alternative:
D1 Package location: `website/` (NOT `site/`, which dlv2-60 reserves for routes.yml and which assemble_public_site.py already uses as its output dir).
D2 Explorer integration: results-explorer stays its own Vite+Preact package served at /results/ with substantial code reuse, not "unchanged". It needs:
- the shared header/shell extracted from App.tsx
- controlled global CSS
- query-string state kept
- deep links to nested /results/ routes on GitHub Pages
- worker/WASM asset paths and recovery verified in a browser
Docs and blog pages never download the Explorer runtime. Embeds come only after cutover (astro-site-60).
D3 URL policy: every URL served today keeps resolving at its current path, `.html` included where practical (docs, /blog/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.html, /blog/atom.xml, /_static/, /_images/). GitHub Pages cannot send HTTP 301s, so redirect pages (meta refresh + canonical) are a last resort and are counted. Pretty URLs are out of scope.
D4 Content source: docs/ stays the only place content is edited until cutover. The site build converts it at build time; converted output is committed only in the cutover PR. The format is plain Markdown by default; MDX is used only where a page needs a component.
D5 Versions: follow the dlv2-60 routes.yml manifest (/docs/ from the latest release tag, /docs/dev/ from trunk). The API reference is release-pinned per adr-independent-publication-authorities (it documents the released wheel, never unreleased develop code). Hosting historical guide versions is a separate, out-of-scope decision.
D6 Layouts: a custom Astro shell for landing, blog and results. For docs, Starlight inside the shared shell is the default; custom docs layouts only if Starlight overrides prove brittle in the spike (G1).
D7 API reference: decided at gate astro-site-02. Authored Markdown API contracts are the source of truth. Docstrings are being deprecated, so no part of the reference may depend on them.
D8 Feed: keep Atom at /blog/atom.xml with unchanged entry ids.
D9 Search: Pagefind for docs and blog HTML only. Results discovery comes from generated static result summaries or a dedicated results lookup (astro-site-61), never from Pagefind over DuckDB-WASM content. Search indexes obey Explorer visibility and withdrawal rules.
D10 Tooling: Node 20 to match CI, an exact lockfile, and no root package.json unless the spike shows workspaces are needed.
D11 Blog drafts: _blog/ (109 md: research, outlines, archives) stays outside every published collection.
D12 Publication: the site plugs into the dlv2-60 site-deploy plane and keeps its artifact boundaries. Explorer code, corpus data, prose and API docs stay separately sourced and pinned, with provenance, privacy checks, route digests, receipts and rollback-by-receipt. The old publication transaction plane is retired by dlv2-62 (an approved decision), not by this migration.
Also list the global guardrails (see context) and the stop conditions for abandoning the migration.
